title: Haile Selassie: Statesman, Colonizer, God?
summary: Josh and Chuck profile Haile Selassie, emperor of Ethiopia, covering his life from birth as Tafari Makonnen through his rise as regent and emperor, the Italian invasions (Battle of Adwa background, 1935-36 occupation, League of Nations appeal), his return in 1941, domestic repression and the 1960 coup attempt, the 1972-75 famine, his 1974 deposition and death, and his posthumous role as a messianic figure in Rastafari and reggae. The episode opens with tour announcements and a short banter intro and closes with a listener mail segment about AP classes.

segments.title: Tour dates and presale announcement
segments.summary: Hosts announce the rest-of-year tour dates, presale codes, and public on-sale date for the live show tour.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter about a song and introduce the episode as a complicated story about Haile Selassie, who is viewed variously as a god, modernizer, and colonizer.

segments.title: Ethiopia background and the Solomonic dynasty
segments.summary: Overview of Ethiopia as a unified-but-diverse nation, its long Christian history, and the Solomonic dynasty claiming descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, with Menelik II unifying the country in the 1880s-1890s.

segments.title: Birth, education and rise of Ras Tafari
segments.summary: Tafari Makonnen's birth in 1892, his royal lineage, education with French missionaries, and his rise through the aristocracy, including becoming de facto ruler under Empress Zewditu.

segments.title: Modernization, League of Nations and coronation as emperor
segments.summary: Tafari's progressive reforms, Ethiopia's 1923 League of Nations membership and slavery abolition pledge, his world tour as Negus, the 1928-30 power struggle with Zewditu, his coronation as emperor, and the first written constitution.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief ad break before the next content segment.

segments.title: Italian invasion and exile
segments.summary: Mussolini's invasion of Ethiopia in 1935 with industrial warfare, the Hoare-Laval Pact, Haile Selassie's League of Nations speech, Time Man of the Year, and his exile in England after the occupation.

segments.title: Return in 1941 and Eritrea
segments.summary: British-backed return in 1941 with Lorenzo Taezaz's guerrilla army, the end of slavery, criticism from Marcus Garvey, and the Eritrea federation and annexation leading to the ELF conflict.

segments.title: 1955 constitution and American tour
segments.summary: The 1955 constitution, Haile Selassie's popularity abroad, and his US visit including a New York ticker tape parade and Yosemite trip, with criticism of his focus on wealthy foreigners.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief ad break and recap of the previous segment's themes.

segments.title: 1960 coup attempt and university
segments.summary: The December 1960 imperial bodyguard coup while Haile Selassie was in Brazil, its suppression, the police-state turn, and the founding of Haile Selassie I University in the former palace.

segments.title: Organization of African Unity
segments.summary: Haile Selassie's role in founding the OAU in 1963 and becoming its first president, and the irony of an unoverthrown monarch leading it.

segments.title: Domestic crackdown and the 1972-75 famine
segments.summary: Rising inflation, repression, the lavish lifestyle including an 80th birthday party, and the famine in Wollo that killed many while food was reportedly exported, and the link between famine regions and unrest.

segments.title: 1974 deposition, Derg rule and death
segments.summary: The 1974 coup by the Derg, Haile Selassie's house arrest and deposition, the monarchy's abolition in 1975, Mengistu's Red Terror, and reports of his death and secret burial under the palace laboratory found in 1992.

segments.title: Rastafari, reggae and Jamaica visit
segments.summary: The Rastafari belief in Haile Selassie as God incarnate, Marcus Garvey's prophecy, the 1966 Jamaica visit, and Rita Marley's conversion, plus reggae's role in shaping his image.

segments.title: Closing thoughts
segments.summary: Hosts reflect on the complexity of Haile Selassie's legacy and how little African history is taught in American schools.

segments.title: Listener mail on AP classes
segments.summary: A high school teacher from suburban Cincinnati writes about AP class access and how he uses the show in his classes.
